questions.q: A farmer in Zaria collects a soil sample that feels gritty, drains quickly and dries out soon after rain. Which soil texture class does the sample most likely belong to?
questions.explanation: The gritty feel, rapid drainage and low water retention are characteristics of sandy soil. Clay soil feels smooth and sticky and retains much water, while loam is a balanced mixture of soil particles.

questions.q: Mangrove trees in the coastal swamps of the Niger Delta develop breathing roots that grow above the mud. This adaptation is mainly to enable the trees to
options: store extra water during dry seasons
anchor themselves in shifting sand dunes
obtain oxygen from the air in waterlogged soil
questions.explanation: Waterlogged mangrove mud contains very little oxygen, so breathing roots take in air from above the mud surface. Prop roots help with support, but the roots described are primarily for gaseous exchange.

questions.q: In a well-developed soil profile, the horizon that contains the highest proportion of humus and plant roots is the
questions.explanation: Topsoil is the surface mineral layer and is richest in humus and plant roots. Subsoil lies below it and generally contains less organic matter, while weathered bedrock and parent rock occur much deeper.

questions.q: When several neighbouring towns grow and merge into one continuous built-up area, the settlement formed is called a
questions.explanation: A conurbation is formed when expanding towns coalesce into a continuous urban region. A satellite town remains physically separate from the main city while depending on it for employment and services.

questions.q: Which latitudinal range best describes the position of mainland Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Mainland Nigeria lies within the tropics, stretching from about 4°N to 14°N. The 4°E to 14°E range describes longitudes rather than latitudes.

questions.q: An aircraft leaves Kano (longitude 8°E) at 10:00 local solar time and flies for 3 hours to a town on longitude 20°W. What is the local solar time at the destination on landing?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 8°E to 20°W, which is 28°. At 4 minutes per degree this is 1 hour 52 minutes; since the destination is west, its local solar time is behind Kano. At landing Kano local solar time is 13:00, so the destination time is 13:00 − 1:52 = 11:08.

questions.q: A cargo ship crosses the International Date Line from the eastern side to the western side at 23:30 on Tuesday, local time. What date and time is it immediately after crossing?
questions.explanation: Crossing the International Date Line from the eastern side to the western side makes the date advance by one day while the clock time stays the same. The time is 23:30 on Tuesday before crossing, so immediately after crossing it is 23:30 on Wednesday. Going in the opposite direction would make the date go back by one day.

questions.q: Which statement best explains why a town at about 70°N can have 24 hours of daylight in June?
options: The Earth is nearest to the Sun in June and therefore receives stronger sunlight.
The Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun and the town lies within the Arctic Circle.
The town rotates more slowly than places near the equator.
The Sun is directly overhead at 70°N in June.
questions.explanation: At about 70°N the town lies inside the Arctic Circle, and in June the Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun. This keeps the Sun above the horizon for the full 24 hours. The distance between the Earth and the Sun is not the cause, and the planet rotates at the same rate at all latitudes.

questions.q: Abandoned pits from artisanal gold mining near Anka, Zamfara State, collect stagnant water and have steep sides. Which action best reduces both mosquito breeding and the danger of children falling into the pits?
options: Converting all the pits into refuse dumps
Backfilling the pits with spoil, grading the land and planting cover vegetation
Fencing each pit and leaving the stagnant water inside
Spraying the water with used engine oil every week
questions.explanation: Backfilling and grading removes the open water and dangerous steep-sided hollows, while planting cover stabilizes the ground. Fencing alone leaves the mosquito breeding water, and oil or refuse dumping adds pollution rather than removing the hazard.

questions.q: Which strategy is most suitable for conserving a threatened monkey population near Afi Mountain while reducing conflict with nearby villagers?
options: Involving villagers in controlled eco-tourism and sustainable gathering of non-timber forest products
Clearing part of the forest for cash crops to create jobs
Banning villagers from the forest without providing alternative livelihoods
Encouraging villagers to capture young monkeys for sale as pets
questions.explanation: Controlled eco-tourism and sustainable non-timber harvesting give villagers an income from the forest without destroying the monkeys' habitat. Exclusion without alternatives or clearing for crops increases conflict and habitat loss, while capturing young monkeys harms the population.

questions.q: Which factor best explains why road transport carries the largest share of goods moved within Nigeria?
options: It offers door-to-door service and reaches many places not served by rail
It has the lowest cost per tonne-kilometre over very long distances
It can carry heavier loads than trains
It is unaffected by weather and poor road conditions
questions.explanation: Road transport is flexible and can collect and deliver goods directly between premises, including areas without rail lines. This door-to-door advantage explains its dominance in internal freight movement. Rail is usually cheaper for very long heavy hauls, and roads are affected by weather and conditions.

questions.q: A country has visible exports of ₦80 million, visible imports of ₦95 million, earnings from services of ₦30 million and payments for services of ₦10 million. What is its balance on the current account?
questions.explanation: Visible trade balance = ₦80 million − ₦95 million = −₦15 million. Net services = ₦30 million − ₦10 million = +₦20 million. Current account balance = −₦15 million + ₦20 million = ₦5 million, which is a surplus.

questions.q: In a limestone cave, a stalactite grows downwards from the roof. Which process is most directly responsible?
options: Evaporation of water leaving behind iron oxide from the rock
Deposition of calcium carbonate as dripping water loses carbon dioxide
Accumulation of fine sand blown into the cave
Erosion of limestone by carbonic acid in dripping water
questions.explanation: When water drips into a cave, it loses carbon dioxide and deposits calcium carbonate, which builds downwards from the roof as a stalactite. Carbonic acid erosion forms cavities rather than adding the hanging deposit, and wind-blown sand is not the main cave material.

questions.q: A river in its lower course builds low ridges of coarse sediment along both banks. Which process is chiefly responsible?
options: Deposition when the river overtops its banks and its velocity falls sharply
Mass movement of saturated soil from the valley sides
Vertical erosion of the river bed
questions.explanation: During a flood the river carries sediment over its banks; as it spreads out, velocity falls and coarse material is deposited along the bank. Repeated floods build these low ridges into levees. Lateral and vertical erosion remove material rather than create bank ridges.

questions.q: On a weather map, lines joining places that receive the same amount of rainfall are called
questions.explanation: Isohyets join places of equal rainfall. Isobars join places of equal atmospheric pressure, isotherms join places of equal temperature, and isohels join places with equal duration of sunshine.

questions.q: At a weather station in Enugu, the air contains 12.0 g of water vapour per cubic metre, while the maximum water vapour the air can hold at that temperature is 20.0 g per cubic metre. What is the relative humidity?
questions.explanation: Relative humidity = (actual vapour content ÷ saturation capacity) × 100% = (12.0 ÷ 20.0) × 100% = 60%. The value 40% would result from using the saturation deficit of 8.0 g/m³ instead of the actual vapour content.

questions.q: A maize farmer in Oyo State has a rectangular field measuring 200 m by 100 m. He plants maize at a spacing of 1 m between plants and 0.5 m between rows. How many maize stands can be accommodated in the field?
questions.explanation: Area of field = 200 m × 100 m = 20,000 m². Area per stand = 1 m × 0.5 m = 0.5 m², so number of stands = 20,000 ÷ 0.5 = 40,000.

questions.q: The main purpose of agricultural extension services in Nigeria is to
options: provide farmers with free land for cultivation
transfer improved farming techniques from research stations to farmers
fix minimum prices for agricultural produce
questions.explanation: Agricultural extension workers educate farmers and spread improved methods, inputs and advice from research institutions. Providing free land, price fixing and tax collection are functions of other agencies, not the main purpose of extension.

questions.q: A sedimentary rock formed from the compaction and cementation of sand grains is
questions.explanation: Sand grains compacted and cemented together form sandstone. Limestone is formed mainly from calcium carbonate, marble is metamorphosed limestone, and granite is an igneous rock.

questions.q: A borehole is on a bearing of 318° from a school. What is the bearing of the school from the borehole?
questions.explanation: The reverse bearing is found by subtracting 180° from 318° because the bearing is greater than 180°. Thus 318° − 180° = 138°. The value 42° comes from subtracting 318° from 360°, which is not the reverse bearing.

questions.q: On a topographic map, closely spaced contour lines indicate a
questions.explanation: Closely spaced contours show that height changes rapidly over a short horizontal distance, which means the land is steep. Widely spaced contours indicate a gentle slope, while a depression is shown by hachures or specially marked contours.

questions.q: A town in Benue State has a mid-year population of 80,000. In that year, 2,400 births and 1,200 deaths are recorded. What is the natural increase rate per 1,000 people?
questions.explanation: Natural increase is births minus deaths: 2,400 − 1,200 = 1,200. The rate per 1,000 is (1,200 ÷ 80,000) × 1,000 = 15 per 1,000. The value 30 per 1,000 is the birth rate alone, while 45 per 1,000 comes from adding births and deaths instead of subtracting.

questions.q: A young teacher leaves a rural community in Ebonyi State for Abuja because of limited schools and irregular payment of salaries. Which factor is mainly responsible for the movement?
options: Push factor in the source area
Pull factor in the destination area
questions.explanation: Limited schools and irregular salaries in the rural source area drive the teacher away, so this is a push factor. A pull factor would be an attraction in Abuja, while net migration is the balance between immigration and emigration.

questions.q: In the humid forest zone of southern Nigeria, heavy rainfall removes soluble mineral salts from the upper soil layer. This process is called
questions.explanation: Leaching is the downward washing of soluble salts from the upper soil by heavy rainfall. Erosion removes solid soil particles, while salinization is the accumulation of salts near the surface.

questions.q: A settlement whose main function is collecting and distributing farm produce from surrounding villages is best described as a
questions.explanation: A market town mainly serves as a collecting and distributing centre for agricultural produce from nearby villages. A dormitory town houses workers who commute elsewhere, an industrial town depends mainly on manufacturing, and a resort town depends on tourism.

questions.q: The process by which an increasing proportion of a country's population comes to live in towns and cities is called
questions.explanation: Urbanization is the rising proportion of a country's population living in towns and cities. Rural–urban migration is the movement of people from villages to towns, while urban sprawl is the outward spreading of built-up areas.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The Moon completes one revolution around the Earth relative to the fixed stars in about
questions.explanation: The sidereal month, measured against the fixed stars, is about 27.3 days. The 29.5-day period is the synodic month, from one new moon to the next, not the revolution relative to the stars.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the Sun appears to move north and south of the equator during the year?
options: The tilt of the Earth's axis as it revolves round the Sun
The varying distance between the Earth and the Sun
The changing speed of the Earth in its orbit
The Earth's rotation on its axis
questions.explanation: The Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5° to the plane of its orbit, so during revolution the overhead noon Sun appears to shift between the tropics. Rotation causes day and night, while distance changes do not produce this yearly north-south shift.

questions.q: The seasonal movement of cattle from the dry Sahel towards the wetter Guinea savanna in Nigeria is known as
questions.explanation: Transhumance is the seasonal movement of livestock between grazing areas, commonly from drier Sahel to wetter savanna in Nigeria. Shifting cultivation is a crop-farming system, while rural-urban migration is movement of people to towns.

questions.q: Ajaokuta, an important iron and steel town, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Ajaokuta, the site of the iron and steel complex, lies in Kogi State on the Niger River. Kwara, Niger and Benue are neighbouring or nearby states but do not contain Ajaokuta.

questions.q: The eastern railway line in Nigeria terminates at which town in the north-east?
questions.explanation: The eastern railway line runs from Port Harcourt through Enugu, Makurdi, Jos and Bauchi to its north-eastern terminus at Maiduguri. Kano is on the western railway system, while Jos and Bauchi are intermediate stations.

questions.q: The local solar time at Cape Town, about longitude 18°E, is 10:00. What is the local solar time at Accra on longitude 0°?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 18°, equivalent to 18 × 4 = 72 minutes. Accra is west of Cape Town, so its local solar time is earlier by 1 hour 12 minutes: 10:00 − 1:12 = 08:48.

questions.q: An aircraft leaves Nairobi on longitude 37°E at a local solar time of 12:00 and flies for 4 hours to Lagos on longitude 3°E. What is the local solar time in Lagos at arrival?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 37° − 3° = 34°, equivalent to 34 × 4 = 136 minutes, or 2 hours 16 minutes. Lagos is west of Nairobi, so at departure its local solar time is 12:00 − 2:16 = 09:44; adding the 4-hour flight gives 13:44.

questions.q: A smallholder near Oyo crops the same plot of maize every year and the yields are declining. Which practice is most likely to restore soil fertility while conserving the soil?
options: Rotate maize with legumes and return crop residues to the soil
Clear the plot and leave it bare throughout the dry season
Apply a single heavy dose of nitrogen fertilizer every five years
Burn all crop residues before planting each season
questions.explanation: Rotating maize with legumes adds nitrogen to the soil, and returning crop residues adds organic matter and protects the surface. Burning residues, leaving soil bare or relying on rare heavy fertilizer doses worsens fertility loss and erosion.

questions.q: An ox-bow lake is most likely to form when
options: a stream sinks into a limestone cavern
a glacier leaves a hollow that becomes filled with water
a river deposits materials at its mouth in distributaries
a meander becomes separated from the main river
questions.explanation: Continued erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner bank of a meander can narrow the neck until the river takes a new course, leaving the old bend as an ox-bow lake. A distributary mouth forms a delta, a glacial hollow may form a tarn, and a sinking stream is associated with limestone drainage.

questions.q: The fan-shaped feature formed where a steep stream deposits its load on a flatter lowland is called
questions.explanation: When a steep stream reaches a gentler slope, its velocity falls and it spreads coarse and fine sediment in a fan shape. A delta forms at a river mouth, while a flood plain and a levee are associated with river channels and overbank deposition.

questions.q: The line separating one drainage basin from another is known as the
questions.explanation: A watershed, also called a water divide, marks the boundary between adjacent drainage basins. A confluence is where two rivers meet, a tributary feeds a larger river, and base level is the lowest level to which a river can erode.

questions.q: The high daytime temperatures recorded in Kano during the dry season are mainly due to
options: strong insolation under mostly cloudless skies
absorption of insolation by abundant water vapour
questions.explanation: In the dry season Kano is dominated by dry Harmattan air with little cloud, so a large proportion of incoming solar radiation reaches and heats the ground. Abundant water vapour and moist maritime air are more characteristic of humid southern areas and would increase cloud and humidity rather than produce this dry-season heating.

questions.q: The instrument used at a weather station to determine wind direction is the
questions.explanation: A wind vane points into the wind and shows the direction from which it blows. An anemometer measures wind speed, a barometer measures atmospheric pressure, and a hygrometer measures humidity.

questions.q: A farmer in Kwara State includes cowpea in a maize rotation mainly because cowpea
options: prevents all insect pests from attacking maize
shades the maize from strong sunlight
adds nitrogen to the soil through root nodules
uses more soil nitrogen than maize
questions.explanation: Cowpea is a legume whose root nodules contain nitrogen-fixing bacteria, so it can improve soil nitrogen for a following maize crop. It does not provide useful shade for maize, it does not remove more nitrogen than it fixes, and it cannot prevent all insect pests.

questions.q: A farmer in Oyo State has a large tomato harvest that cannot be sold immediately. Which practice would best reduce post-harvest loss?
options: Leaving the fruits uncovered in direct sunlight
Processing the tomatoes into paste or dried products
Packing the fruits in a single heap in the open
Delaying harvest until all the fruits become over-ripe
questions.explanation: Processing tomatoes into paste or drying them reduces moisture and extends their storage life, so less of the harvest spoils before sale. Heaping the fruits in the open, exposing them to direct sun, or delaying harvest until they are over-ripe all encourage rapid deterioration.

questions.q: The treatment and bottling of spring water for sale is best classified as
questions.explanation: Treating and bottling spring water changes a raw material into a packaged manufactured product, which makes it a secondary activity. Primary activities extract directly from nature, while tertiary activities provide services.

questions.q: Which industry is best located close to its market because its finished product is bulky and perishable?
questions.explanation: Bread is bulky and spoils quickly, so bakeries need to be close to consumers. Cement, sugar refining and iron smelting are more closely tied to raw materials or heavy inputs.

questions.q: The property of a mineral that describes the way light is reflected from its surface is called
questions.explanation: Lustre is the appearance of a mineral's surface in reflected light, such as metallic or vitreous. Cleavage describes how it breaks, streak is the colour of its powder, and hardness is resistance to scratching.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:75,000, a straight footpath measures 8.4 cm. What is its length on the ground?
questions.explanation: Multiply the map distance by the scale: 8.4 cm × 75,000 = 630,000 cm. Since 100,000 cm = 1 km, the ground distance is 6.3 km.

questions.q: A clinic is on a bearing of 198° from a school. What is the bearing of the school from the clinic?
questions.explanation: The bearing of one point from another differs by 180° from its reciprocal. Thus 198° − 180° = 18°, written as 018°. Subtracting 198° from 360° gives 162°, which is not the back bearing.

questions.q: In a local government area, there are 12,000 males and 15,000 females. What is the sex ratio of the population?
questions.explanation: Sex ratio is usually expressed as males per 100 females: (12,000 ÷ 15,000) × 100 = 80. The value 125 would be females per 100 males, not the requested ratio.

questions.q: The movement of people from a city to smaller towns and rural areas around it is best described as
questions.explanation: Counter-urbanisation is the movement of people out of large cities into smaller towns and rural areas. Rural-urban migration is the opposite movement, and transhumance is the seasonal movement of livestock.

questions.q: A school farm at Ijebu-Ode has a sandy soil that dries out quickly after rain. Which practice would best improve the soil's water-holding capacity for vegetable production?
options: burning crop residues on the plot before planting
incorporating well-decomposed organic manure into the soil
adding more coarse river sand to the plot
planting only shallow-rooted crops every season
questions.explanation: Well-decomposed organic manure improves soil aggregation and increases the number of fine pores, so the sandy soil retains more moisture without becoming waterlogged. Adding coarse river sand would increase drainage and worsen drying out, while burning residues destroys organic matter.

questions.q: After several seasons of dry-season irrigation with slightly saline borehole water in Katsina, a farmer finds a white crust on the surface of the field. The soil problem is most likely
questions.explanation: Repeated irrigation with slightly saline water in a hot dry climate can raise salts to the surface as water evaporates, forming a white crust. This process is salinisation; leaching would remove soluble salts rather than concentrate them near the surface.
